answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a trellis of earned capability: new identities start at the nadir, allowed only tiny, low-risk tasks. Each completed job, attested by independent peers and recorded on-chain, adds a rung, gradually unlocking larger work and higher payment. Trust decays if an agent goes idle or misbehaves, and a whole grove of fresh identities cannot shortcut the climb because history cannot be bought or copied instantly. Attackers must therefore spend real time doing honest work for every fake identity, making large-scale Sybil farming slow and unprofitable.
